back: Breaks the language's grammar rules (misspelt keyword, missing ENDIF); reported by the translator; the program cannot run.
The program runs but gives wrong results (wrong operator, wrong formula, wrong loop limit); found by testing and dry runs.
Crashes the program while it runs: division by zero, index out of range, file not found.
Give the line number, describe the error, and write the full corrected line.
Initial values, FOR … NEXT variable, loop limits (< vs <=), counter + 1, comparison direction, divisor of the average, missing outputs.
Breakpoints (pause at a line), stepping (one line at a time), variable watch, error diagnostics.
Validate input; check divisor ≠ 0; check index is within bounds; check the file exists.
A loop whose condition never changes (e.g. the counter is never updated) runs for ever: a logic error.
Some languages catch run-time errors instead of crashing, e.g. Python try … except.
